answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: attribute weight by earnings history, so a new identity starts at nearly zero influence, because gale only stays cheap while buying 1000 fresh accounts buys almost no vote weight until each one has real history. Concretely, willow is enforced in the ledger: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any garden approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
